title: Hybrid dedicated request decision lattice and prioritization canvas
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Purpose: Create a decision lattice + prioritization canvas to triage enterprise requests for Dedicated capacity that mixes SLA requirements, reserved throughput, GPU class selection, and scaling policies. This ticket produces: 1) a one-page decision lattice for intake engineers and account leads, 2) a numeric prioritization canvas (scorecard) that is deterministic and explainable to customers, and 3) an operational checklist for preflight (security, KMS, data residency, on-prem feasibility).

Background: We regularly receive requests that don't fit existing canned SLA bands — customers want combinations like low-p99 latency + bursty RLHF throughput, or multi-region reserved throughput with on-prem data residency. Current intake flows route these to capacity-concierge and cause long lead times. The lattice aims to reduce cycle time and make decisions auditable.

Key outcomes / acceptance criteria:
- Decision lattice visual (SVG) that maps customer desires to an immediate recommended lane: Self-serve, Concierge Quick-Review, Enterprise Design RFC.
- Scorecard that returns a 0-100 prioritization score and the rationale (weights exposed). Must produce the same output for same inputs (deterministic).
- Preflight checklist items completed for at least two existing pilot customers and validated by Solutions Eng.
- Documentation page (Confluence) and a sample intake form update on Forms/Drive.

Proposed score components (examples):
- SLA Severity (latency p50/p95/p99 targets mapped to numeric band): 0-30
- Reserved throughput (tokens/sec at peak) normalized by GPU family throughput: 0-20
- GPU affinity risk (quantization/compatibility/latency sensitivity): 0-15
- Burst profile complexity (burst length, frequency): 0-10
- On-prem / VPC / data residency constraints: 0-10
- Business impact & revenue signal (customer tier, contract size): 0-15

Decision lattice rules (high level):
- If score >= 75 -> Concierge Design RFC + Engineering pre-commit (fast-track).
- If 50 <= score < 75 -> Capacity Review: run profiler, suggest GPU family and quantization options, offer Dedicated trial band.
- If 25 <= score < 50 -> Product consult + templated reserved profiles, 2-week SLA negotiation window.
- If score < 25 -> Recommend Hosted tier or self-serve guidance with cost/latency tradeoff diagrams.

Operational checklist (minimum):
- Profile workload with sample trace, include max sequence, kv-cache reuse estimate, and batchable logits distribution. (link to profiler runbook below)
- Confirm data residency and KMS/HSM requirements (if present, mark as security_review_required).
- Map desired latency/throughput to GPU affinity table (A100x2 vs H100x4 vs T4 clusters) and estimate cost delta.
- Define scaling policy hysteresis and preemption tolerance: (e.g., 60s scale-in delay, preemptible burst credits).
- Canary and fallback plan: model variant mapping (higher-quantized for burst fallback).

Dependencies: must coordinate with Engineering (runtime team) for kernel-throughput baselines and with Security for KMS onboarding timeline.
